dx.paper: Ribeiro AH et al. Automatic diagnosis of the 12-lead ECG using a deep neural network. Nat Commun 2020;11:1760

age.paper: Lima EM et al. Deep neural network-estimated electrocardiographic age as a mortality predictor. Nat Commun 2021;12:5117

thresholds_note: The probability above which each abnormality is reported. Recovered from the authors' published decisions on CODE-test: at these values our port agrees with them on 99.6-100% of tracings per class.
weights_note: How far a reported abnormality moves the score, out of 100: atrial fibrillation and left bundle branch block warrant senior review on their own; a right bundle branch block or first-degree block an adjusted look; sinus brady- or tachycardia are usually situational and only a prompt.
dx_validation: our PyTorch port on CODE-test (827 ECGs, cardiologist labels): AUC 0.994 1dAVb, 0.999 RBBB, 1.000 LBBB, 0.997 SB, 0.997 AF, 0.999 ST; F1 at the authors' thresholds 0.84 / 0.94 / 1.00 / 0.86 / 0.78 / 0.95. Brazilian cohort, NOT validated in South Asia
age_validation: our run on CODE-test (827 ECGs): MAE 11.6 y, r 0.60, mean error +4.6 y; the published figure is 8.4 y on CODE-15%. Reads young adults about 15 y older and the over-80s about 10 y younger, so the gap is shown against what the model reads for a typical person of that age, and it is a prompt, never a score

age_calibration.note: Least-squares fit of the model's output against true age on CODE-test: expected_ecg_age = slope * age + intercept. The reported gap is ecg_age - expected_ecg_age.
